newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo says Frisinger a chairman candidate.
newsitem.headline: Volvo says Frisinger a chairman candidate.

text.p: Swedish automotive group AB Volvo said on Wednesday its board member and former chief executive Hakan Frisinger is a candidate for the chairman post, replacing Bert-Olof Svanholm who has died.
"Hakan Frisinger is one of the possible candidates for the chairman post," Jonas Winzell at Volvo's investor relations told Reuters.

"There are strong reasons to believe that Frisinger will take over the chairman's gavel until the annual general shareholders' meeting...But I want to await the press release which will be sent later in the day."

Svanholm's death was announced on Tuesday and business daily Dagens Industri reported on Wednesday that Hakan Frisinger would be appointed temporary chairman and was likely to assume the permanent position.
Frisinger, 69, was Volvo's chief executive between 1983 and 1987.

Volvo's board will meet around midday on Wednesday. Apart from appointing a temporary chairman it will also decide on details about the redemption of five percent of shares, which the company announced when releasing 1996 earnings.
